references.text: Moses promises that the Lord will keep diseases away from Israel if they keep His commandments, especially the diseases that struck Egypt.
The blessings that follow from listening to the Lord's voice and keeping His commandments, including protection from disease.
A warning that the diseases of Egypt will come upon Israel if they do not obey the Lord.
The Lord promises to remove sickness from the people when they serve Him.
The psalm praises the Lord as He who heals all your diseases and affirms God's role as healer (JHVH Rofe).
The Lord heals those with a broken heart and binds up their wounds.
The prophecy about the Lord's servant who was wounded for our transgressions, and by whose stripes we are healed.
The Lord promises to give health and heal Israel's wounds.
The Lord calls for repentance and promises life to those who keep His laws and commandments.
Jesus heals the sick and fulfills the prophecy that He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.
An encouragement to pray for the sick with a promise of healing from the Lord.
Christ bore our sins on the cross, and by His wounds we have been healed.
Both verses link the identity 'the Lord your God' directly to the requirement to cast away Egyptian idols to avoid judgment of uncleanness.
A direct theological and textual parallel where Deuteronomy confirms and expands upon the promise of protection from Egyptian diseases conditioned on obedience.
A contrasting parallel where Judges shows a historical breach of the same condition of obedience that Exodus 15:26 sets for God's protection.
A literal textual parallel where Deuteronomy 13:19 reuses the exact conditions from Exodus 15:26 for the covenant blessing.
A strong thematic parallel where Deuteronomy 28:1 expands the principle of obedience from healing to national supremacy with the same linguistic structure.
